prompt.context: Your client, Erween Mills, is a palm oil mill based out of Guatemala. The mill extracts crude oil from fresh palm fruit and then sells it in the commodity market. Erween Mills competes with a nearby mill for palm fruit, and producers sell fruit to the highest bidder. Palm oil is edible vegetable oil that trades as a commodity and is the only product currently sold by the mill. The mill has steady revenue, but capacity utilization has been decreasing year over year. The mill is struggling financially and needs a solution as soon as possible.
prompt.question: Erween Mills has been facing profitability problems for the past couple of years. Please help identify the root cause(s) and recommend ways to improve the mill's profitability.

clarifying_info.q: What is a palm oil mill?
clarifying_info.a: A palm oil mill extracts crude oil from fresh palm fruit and then sells it in the commodity market.
The client competes with a nearby mill for palm fruit; producers sell fruit to the highest bidder.

clarifying_info.q: What products does Erween Mills sell?
clarifying_info.a: Palm oil is the only product currently sold by the mill. It is edible vegetable oil and trades as a commodity.
The mill has steady revenue, but capacity utilization has been decreasing year over year.

exhibits.title: Operating Expenses ($M)
exhibits.shows: Stacked bar chart of annual operating expenses from 2018 to 2021, broken into four cost categories: Raw Materials, Machinery Operations, SG&A, and Labor.
exhibits.data: 2018: Raw Materials $13M, Machinery Ops $6M, SG&A $5M, Labor $4M | 2019: Raw Materials $22M, Machinery Ops $7M, SG&A $5M, Labor $5M | 2020: Raw Materials $35M, Machinery Ops $5M, SG&A $5M, Labor $4M | 2021: Raw Materials $36M, Machinery Ops $9M, SG&A $6M, Labor $5M

exhibits.title: Palm Fruit Supplier Map
exhibits.shows: Map showing the mill's location relative to four potential palm fruit suppliers at varying distances, with each supplier's material cost per ton listed. Supplier C has an additional import duty of 5%.
exhibits.data: Supplier A: $175/ton, 50 miles | Supplier B: $140/ton, 75 miles | Supplier C: $112/ton, 105 miles, 5% import duty | Supplier D: $124/ton, 220 miles

exhibits.title: Equipment Options Comparison
exhibits.shows: Table comparing three scenarios (Current equipment, New equipment at $500K investment, Overhaul at $300K investment) across production volume, raw material cost per ton, raw material savings percentage, maintenance cost per incident, and maintenance frequency per year. Note: for the current machine, raw material to finished product ratio is 1:1.
exhibits.data: Current: 50,000 tons, $35/ton raw material, 0% savings, $10,000 maintenance x3/yr | New ($500K): 50,000 tons, $35/ton, 20% raw material savings, $5,000 maintenance x3/yr | Overhaul ($300K): 50,000 tons, $35/ton, 15% raw material savings, $6,000 maintenance x4/yr

framework: Revenues: delta in units sold, delta in commodity price, change in product mix (grades of palm oil)
Costs: change in COGS (raw material costs), change in value chain costs, change in machinery efficiency and maintenance costs, change in fixed costs (rent, SG&A, labor)

Market and Regulations: change in tax rates or import duties, regulatory changes making quality checks more stringent, political volatility shifting supply/demand, substitutes being scaled and commercialized, small mills creating local monopolies

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 1, what is driving the profitability decline at Erween Mills?
questions.guidance: A good candidate will observe that raw material costs have increased rapidly — nearly 3x from 2018 to 2021 ($13M to $36M). An excellent candidate will also flag that machinery/PP&E costs roughly doubled (from ~$6M to ~$9M), while labor and SG&A remained relatively stable. The candidate should conclude that raw material sourcing and machinery operations are the two priority areas to investigate.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, which supplier should Erween Mills select? Calculate the total cost per ton for each supplier.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate total landed cost per ton = material cost + transportation cost + VAT on material cost + import duty if applicable. The lowest total cost supplier is the recommendation. Candidate should ask for or be told: last year's supply = 1,500 tons; shipping = $1.6/ton/mile; VAT = 12.5% applied to raw material cost only; import duty for Supplier C = 5% applied to overall cost.

math.setup: Total cost per ton = Material cost + (Distance x $1.6/mile) + (12.5% x Material cost) + Import duty if applicable
steps: Ranking: Supplier A ($276.88) < Supplier B ($277.50) < Supplier C ($308.70) < Supplier D ($491.50)
math.answer: Supplier A has the lowest total landed cost at approximately $276.88/ton, followed closely by Supplier B at $277.50/ton. Supplier D is by far the most expensive due to the 220-mile distance.

questions.prompt: Erween Mills is considering two options to reduce machinery operations cost: (1) Purchase new equipment for $500K, or (2) Overhaul existing equipment for $300K. Using Exhibit 3, which option should they choose and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate total annual operating cost (raw material + maintenance) for each scenario, derive annual savings vs. current, then compute 3-year ROI = (3-year total savings - investment) / investment. Overhaul has a higher 3-year ROI (~169%) than new equipment (~119%) and should be recommended. Throughput is the same at 50,000 tons for all three scenarios; savings come from reduced raw material needed.

math.setup: Total annual cost = (Production volume x (1 - savings%) x $35/ton) + (Maintenance cost x Frequency). ROI (3 years) = (3 x Annual savings - Investment) / Investment
steps: Current: Raw material = 50,000 x $35 = $1,750,000; Maintenance = $10,000 x 3 = $30,000; Total = $1,780,000
math.answer: Overhaul has a 3-year ROI of ~169% vs. ~119% for new equipment. Despite generating lower annual savings, the much lower investment makes overhauling the superior choice on an ROI basis.

recommendation: Start a contract with Supplier A (lowest total landed cost ~$276.88/ton) to reduce raw material costs, which have grown to ~3x 2018 levels and are the primary profitability driver
Overhaul existing mill machinery to reduce machinery operations costs, with a projected 3-year ROI of approximately 169%
risks: Quality and reliability concerns when switching to a new supplier
Overhaul implementation risks and potential delays that could reduce throughput during execution
Demand volatility of palm oil as a commodity
next_steps: Move 10-15% of sourcing to the new supplier initially to test quality and reliability before full commitment
Build a robust execution plan for a fast machinery overhaul with minimal downtime
Monitor capacity utilization trends and re-evaluate revenue levers (pricing, product mix) as cost structure improves
